key_insight: Verified runtime experiences can be consolidated into reusable procedural knowledge, but smaller models may need that knowledge concretized before it improves performance.
engineering_relevance: For scientific computing and fracture/damage workflows, the method suggests a path from one-off solver feedback to durable assistant behavior that can generalize across tasks.
method: Contrast verified successes and failures to extract cross-task procedures.
Use a development-validation gate plus failure-informed, answer-free query synthesis to grow consolidation data.
Have a stronger teacher concretize procedures into executable code for procedure-free SFT, with a no-procedure control for comparison.
evidence_signal: On SciCode, procedure injection improved Qwen3.6-27B by +3.85/+6.26 sub-step/main-problem points, while the 9B student only improved after procedure-guided concretization (+3.89/+6.25 over control; +5.62/+11.25 over baseline).
watch_item: The approach depends on a stronger model to bridge the abstraction-execution gap, so gains may not transfer if the student cannot reliably operationalize abstract procedures.
paper_title: From Execution to Capability: Scientific Experience Consolidation via Procedural Knowledge Synthesis
